---
title: "{{< fa terminal >}} Step 4: Install Claude Code"
---

Claude Code is the coding agent we use on the day. It runs in a terminal, reads and writes files in a project folder, and runs commands, which is what makes it an agent rather than a chat window.

::: {.callout-important}
## Account and plan: confirmed nearer the time

The group is arranging access, including who pays and under which plan. That decision was not settled when this page was written, and it changes the sign-in step and, more importantly, the rules about what data you may put into the tool.

**You will get an email with the account details before {{< var due.setup >}}.** Install the software now by following the steps below, and sign in when the email arrives. If you already have a personal Claude account, do not use it for workshop data until you have read the section on data at the bottom of this page.
:::

## {{< fa download >}} Install

Claude Code needs Node.js version 18 or newer.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

Open Terminal and run:

```bash
node --version
```

If that reports a version below 18, or says the command is not found, install Node.js from <https://nodejs.org/> (choose the LTS version) and try again.

Then install Claude Code:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

### Windows

Claude Code runs under Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). Open PowerShell as administrator and run:

```powershell
wsl --install
```

Restart when prompted. Then open the Ubuntu terminal that was installed, and inside it check Node.js:

```bash
node --version
```

If the version is below 18 or the command is not found, follow the instructions at <https://nodejs.org/> for Linux, then install Claude Code:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

### Linux

Open a terminal and run:

```bash
node --version
```

If that reports a version below 18, install Node.js from <https://nodejs.org/>. Then:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

:::

## {{< fa circle-check >}} Check the install worked

```bash
claude --version
```

That should print a version number. If it prints an error instead, do not keep trying variations. Go to [Step 5](05-verify-setup.qmd), which explains how to report the problem so it can be fixed before the workshop.

## {{< fa shield-halved >}} What data may go into the tool

This part does not depend on the plan decision, and it holds regardless:

::: {.callout-important}
## The group rule

Personal and sensitive data never go into a Git repository, private repositories included. The same rule covers the agent: Claude Code reads whole directories and sends file contents to a model, so anything sitting in your project folder can leave your machine.
:::

ETH treats AI systems as external cloud services. At most "confidential" data may go into a cleared cloud service, and "strictly confidential" data never leaves ETH. You stay responsible for the output, you declare AI use, and you check every result.

The plan you are on matters here. On consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max), Anthropic may use conversations and coding sessions to train models under four conditions: you allow it in privacy settings, a conversation is flagged for safety review, you send feedback with the thumbs buttons, or you opt in to a tester program. Commercial plans fall under a separate policy where the customer controls the data. This split is exactly why the group is arranging access rather than asking everyone to sign up individually.

The dataset you picked in [Step 1](01-bring-your-data.qmd) is openly shareable, so none of this restricts what we do on the day. It restricts what you do with the tool afterwards, which is the more important case.

## {{< fa circle-question >}} Optional: an editor

You do not need one. Claude Code runs in a terminal on its own, and that is how we will use it.

If you would rather see your files alongside it, both [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) and [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) have integrated terminals that work fine. Use whatever you already have. Do not install a new editor for this workshop.
